nodes.label: Managed Credential Binding
nodes.rationale: Trust boundary where the runtime injects GitHub App credentials via destination-bound managed HTTP bindings, keeping tokens out of GraphML and input payloads.

nodes.label: Project Transition Behavior
nodes.rationale: Implements optimistic CAS safety for GitHub Project v2 items using absolute writes, durable intent, and remote reread to handle lack of atomic conditional updates.

nodes.label: Release Prepare Behavior
nodes.rationale: Read-only behavior that verifies release branch head and parses Maven version to generate advisory release metadata without mutating GitHub state.

nodes.label: Authenticated Webhook Relay
nodes.rationale: Operator-managed relay that forwards GitHub webhooks to Ravenroot with HMAC verification, ensuring body integrity and replay protection.

nodes.label: Durable Bundle State and Audit Evidence
nodes.norm_label: durable bundle state and audit evidence
nodes.rationale: Operator-owned SQLite file; forward-only schema migration; operations partitioned by tenant/profile/kind/key, content-bound by SHA-256, protected by expiring single-writer lease; audit table stores only structural keys and evidence digests.

nodes.label: Managed HTTP Credential Binding
nodes.rationale: Runtime injects GitHub App installation credentials through destination-bound managed HTTP credential binding; only webhook verification uses raw credential resolution with short-lived lease erased after HMAC computation.

nodes.label: Ravenroot GitHub Automation Bundle
nodes.rationale: Optional Node SDK /2 bundle contributing five behaviors: github-events-source, project-transition, github-app-review, github-workflow-watch, and release-prepare.

nodes.label: Ravenroot GitHub Automation Extension Bundle
nodes.rationale: Optional Node SDK /2 bundle contributing exactly five behaviors; not part of default distribution; operator builds, installs, enables, profiles, and grants explicitly.

nodes.label: Managed HTTP Signing Composition
nodes.rationale: Core resolves credentials once per invocation, signs exact outgoing bytes, and clears them; extension never sees access keys or secrets.

nodes.label: object.delete Operation
nodes.rationale: Deletes object with optional versionId; 200/204 returns DELETED, 404 returns NOT_FOUND; no automatic retry; recovery.repeatable is opt-in.

nodes.label: object.get Operation
nodes.rationale: Reads object with encoding (text/base64), maxBytes, timeoutMs, maxConcurrency; result includes ETag, version id, bytes, SHA-256.

nodes.label: object.list Operation
nodes.rationale: Lists objects with prefix, maxResults, projection, retries; cursor is versioned envelope with tenant/scope digest; XML parsing is hardened.

nodes.label: object.put Operation
nodes.rationale: Writes object with optional contentType, ifMatch, ifNoneMatch; result includes ETag, version id, bytes.

nodes.label: Storage Profile Configuration
nodes.rationale: Operator-defined JSON profile specifying origin, region, bucket, keyPrefix, operations allowlist, and ceilings; bound via RAVENROOT_OBJECT_STORAGE_PROFILE_<HEX_PROFILE>.

nodes.label: Object Operations (Get/Put/List/Delete)
nodes.rationale: The four core S3-compatible operations exposed by the extension, each with specific payload structures, result schemas, and retry/recovery semantics.

nodes.label: Recovery and Retry Semantics
nodes.rationale: Fail-closed recovery model where mutations (PUT/DELETE) are not automatically retried on ambiguity, and LIST retries are bounded and rate-limited. Explicit 'repeatable' declaration required for retry.

nodes.label: Security and Validation Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Strict validation rules including UTF-8 path restrictions, byte ceilings, deadline enforcement, XML hardening, and credential isolation to prevent traversal, injection, and data leakage.

nodes.label: Ravenroot S3-compatible Object Storage Extension
nodes.rationale: Opt-in Node SDK /2 plugin contributing object.get, object.put, object.list, object.delete; not part of default distribution.

nodes.label: Ravenroot Object Storage Extension
nodes.rationale: Opt-in Node SDK plugin providing S3-compatible object storage operations (get, put, list, delete) with managed signing and strict security boundaries.

nodes.label: Release Publication Job
nodes.rationale: Handles the actual distribution of artifacts to Maven Central, GHCR, and GitHub Releases, including signing, attestation, and idempotent publishing.

nodes.label: Release Validation Job
nodes.rationale: Executes comprehensive pre-flight checks including tag ancestry, version surface consistency, and build verification to establish a trusted baseline.

nodes.label: Public Release Verification Job
nodes.rationale: Performs anonymous verification of published artifacts to confirm they are accessible and immutable without requiring credentials.

nodes.label: Release Contract Validator
nodes.rationale: Python script enforcing release event contracts, tag ancestry, and authorization checks to prevent unauthorized or inconsistent releases.

nodes.label: Publish Immutable Release Workflow
nodes.rationale: Orchestrates the end-to-end immutable release lifecycle, enforcing strict validation gates before any external publication to ensure supply chain integrity.

nodes.label: Matrix Configuration Schema
nodes.rationale: Base64-encoded JSON configuration defining store, profiles, credentials, and operational limits.

nodes.label: matrix.send Operation
nodes.rationale: Idempotent room message sending operation using Matrix transaction path, returning bounded content-free results.

nodes.label: Matrix Client-Server API
nodes.rationale: External protocol specification for /sync and room event send endpoints.

nodes.label: matrix.sync Operation
nodes.rationale: Deployment-owned long-poll source for receiving bounded room timeline events using Client-Server /sync endpoint.

nodes.label: Ravenroot Node SDK
nodes.rationale: Target SDK version 2 that the Matrix package integrates with.

nodes.label: Cursor Scoping & Persistence
nodes.rationale: Cursors scoped by tenant, profile, deployment, and node; prevents cross-deployment cursor advancement; durable-ingress receipt required before cursor advance.

nodes.label: Initial Sync Modes
nodes.rationale: Defines 'skip' (checkpoint without delivery) and 'deliver-bounded' (deliver first page) modes; fails closed on limited/over-cap pages to prevent silent gap advancement.

nodes.label: Security & Credential Model
nodes.rationale: Package never constructs Authorization header; managed HTTP service injects tenant-scoped token after policy checks; SQLite stores no tokens or message bodies.

nodes.label: Ravenroot Matrix Extension
nodes.rationale: Optional node package for Matrix Client-Server API integration, providing message sending and timeline synchronization.

nodes.label: Matrix Client-Server API Spec
nodes.rationale: External protocol reference for /sync, room event send, and unsigned event data structures.

nodes.label: Fixed Evaluation Budgets
nodes.rationale: 2,048 expression characters, 4,096 UTF-8 bytes, 128 AST nodes, depth 16, 2,048 operations, 256 entries per collection, 4,096 values, 64 KiB text, 1 MiB canonical encoding, one selection/projection, 32 global and 8 per-node evaluations, one-second deadline.

nodes.label: Expression Root Payload
nodes.rationale: Exactly the incoming canonical payload: null, Boolean, signed 64-bit integer, finite double, text, or recursively bounded maps and lists.

nodes.label: SPEL Failure Codes
nodes.rationale: Stable codes: SPEL_EXPRESSION_MISSING, SPEL_EXPRESSION_TOO_LONG, SPEL_EXPRESSION_INVALID, SPEL_AST_UNSUPPORTED, SPEL_AST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, SPEL_FORBIDDEN_PROPERTY, SPEL_INPUT_REJECTED, SPEL_RESULT_REJECTED, SPEL_DECISION_NOT_BOOLEAN, SPEL_CAPACITY_UNAVAILABLE, SPEL_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, SPEL_EVALUATION_FAILED.

nodes.label: Restricted SpEL Security Policy
nodes.rationale: Deliberately does not expose variables, functions, methods, Java types, constructors, beans, assignment, arithmetic, regex, reflection, application objects, attributes, environment, filesystem, or network access. Refuses class, getClass, metaClass, classLoader, declaringClass, protectionDomain, __proto__, prototype, and constructor case-insensitively.

nodes.label: spel.decision Node
nodes.rationale: Requires expression; optionally accepts trueOutcome/falseOutcome; preserves payload and attributes; selects one outcome.

nodes.label: spel.transform Node
nodes.rationale: Requires only expression; bounded result replaces payload, attributes pass through, emits continue.

nodes.label: SPEL Error Codes
nodes.rationale: Stable public failure codes used for all evaluation, capacity, and deadline errors.

nodes.label: Fixed Resource Budgets
nodes.rationale: Hard limits on expression size, AST complexity, collection entries, and execution time to ensure fail-fast behavior.

nodes.label: ai.ravenroot.extensions.spel Package
nodes.rationale: Optional migration package contributing spel.transform and spel.decision; not part of core or default distribution.

nodes.label: Ravenroot SpEL Extension
nodes.rationale: Optional migration package providing restricted SpEL evaluation capabilities, distinct from Ravenroot core.

nodes.label: Bundle Catalog
nodes.rationale: The set of optional first-party bundles (AI, AMQP, Discord, Filesystem, Git workspace, GitHub automation, JDBC, Kafka, Mail, Matrix, Mattermost, Object storage, OCR, OpenAPI client/server, Slack, SpEL, Teams, Telegram, WebSocket) and their nodes.

nodes.label: openapi.receive Source
nodes.rationale: Asynchronous durable ingress contract; normalizes requests as openapi.request.v1 and offers via TrustedIngress.offerDurably; returns 202 only for DurablyCommitted or Duplicate.

nodes.label: openapi.request-reply Source
nodes.rationale: Synchronous request/reply behavior; admits one live traversal through RequestReplyIngress; retains capacity until terminal; process-local registry supporting single live replica.

nodes.label: Operator Configuration Contract
nodes.rationale: RAVENROOT_OPENAPI_SERVER_CONFIG env var with strict JSON Base64; authority, projection, and profiles fix scopes, ceilings, and OpenAPI spec SHA-256; environment compiler refuses disagreement.

nodes.label: RequestReplyIngress
nodes.rationale: Generation-fenced ingress for synchronous exchanges; runtime RequestReplyLimits are authoritative and can be stricter than profile or HTTP ceilings.

nodes.label: Telemetry Policy
nodes.rationale: Version 1 emits no package-specific metrics or logs; managed-route inventory exposes only package, route, generation, and state; no tenant or request content in metrics.

nodes.label: TrustedIngress
nodes.rationale: Core mechanism for durable asynchronous custody; single-replica durability qualification applies.

nodes.label: OpenAPI Specification Validation
nodes.rationale: Strict JSON 3.0.3 validation supporting bounded schema subset, rejecting YAML, 3.1, server overrides, external references, and vendor extensions at source start.

nodes.label: Operator Configuration
nodes.rationale: Configuration via RAVENROOT_OPENAPI_SERVER_CONFIG environment variable containing authority, projection, and profiles with strict JSON validation and SHA-256 pinned OpenAPI documents.

nodes.label: Ravenroot OpenAPI Server Extension
nodes.rationale: Optional Node SDK /2 plugin contributing deployment-scoped sources openapi.receive and openapi.request-reply; exposes no listener and imports no server implementation.

nodes.label: Operator-Owned Profile Configuration
nodes.rationale: 13-field semicolon-separated profile resolved from environment variables; tokens resolved per-invocation for rotation support.

nodes.label: Rolling Rate Limiter
nodes.rationale: Per-process rolling one-second window using System.nanoTime; fail-closed quarantine on clock discontinuities; generation-checked linearization.

nodes.label: telegram.answer.callback Behavior
nodes.rationale: Acknowledges callback queries to prevent client progress indicators; uses bounded tenant/profile/callback registry to prevent duplicates.

nodes.label: telegram.delete.message Behavior
nodes.rationale: Explicit deletion subject to Telegram's 48-hour limit and bot permission rules.

nodes.label: telegram.edit.message Behavior
nodes.rationale: Explicit text, caption, or markup edits; never substitutes a send on failure.

nodes.label: telegram.send Behavior
nodes.rationale: Bounded send supporting text, photos, and inline keyboards with profile-enforced limits.

nodes.label: Receive-Acknowledge-Act Callback Flow
nodes.rationale: Normalizes inbound callback, immediately invokes answer.callback, then runs slower work and optionally edit/send; keeps acknowledgement latency independent of downstream work.

nodes.label: Per-Process Rolling Rate Limiter
nodes.rationale: Exact one-second rolling window driven by System.nanoTime; fail-closed quarantine on clock discontinuity; generation-checked linearization prevents delayed ticker samples from corrupting live rate state.

nodes.label: Ravenroot Telegram Extension
nodes.rationale: Source-installable Node SDK package contributing four Telegram Bot API behaviors; deliberately excluded from standard image.

nodes.label: Operator-configured nodes
nodes.rationale: Nodes that require specific operator profiles (e.g., ai.llm-profile, amqp.profile) and can select bundle.service-grant.

nodes.label: AMQP Exercise
nodes.rationale: Sanitized end-to-end exercise that builds the AMQP plugin on the producer side, transfers the closed bundle in the .rrcfg, applies it to a temporary real Compose target, proves restart by container identity, checks AMQP behaviors, verifies readiness and idempotent reapply, then performs and verifies rollback.

nodes.label: Apply Transaction
nodes.rationale: Writes only .ravenroot-config/ beneath target; refuses identity changes, drift, incompatible bundles, digest failures, missing payloads, and interrupted transactions; backs up managed files, writes a mode 0600 durable mutation journal, and restores previous bytes on failure with reverse-order compensation.

nodes.label: Bundle Service Grant
nodes.rationale: Optional profiles requesting managed services require a bundle.service-grant selection keyed by the exact plugin manifest ID; the packager refuses a missing or unrelated grant so the installed carrier cannot be silently omitted.

nodes.label: CLI Interface
nodes.rationale: Exposes contracts, pack, inspect, plan, apply, verify, and rollback commands; uses --password-stdin for encrypted embedded secrets and RAVENROOT_CONFIG_VERIFY_BEARER for verification bearer.

nodes.label: Compose Target
nodes.rationale: Writes an additive override, mounts generated operator documents read only, stages prebuilt bundles into the existing image build, recreates only ravenroot, and verifies the rendered model plus the running container environment.

nodes.label: Kubernetes Target
nodes.rationale: Writes target-owned Secrets, Helm image values, and an additive strategic Deployment patch; mounts generated documents, builds an optional derived image, performs the Helm upgrade, applies the patch, waits for rollout, and verifies live Secret data, references, mounts, image, release, and availability.

nodes.label: .rrcfg Package Contract
nodes.rationale: Version-one deterministic ZIP container with canonical manifest, target/tenant binding, selected contracts, required capabilities, bundle manifests, redacted plan, and SHA-256 size bindings; embedded secrets use Argon2id and AES-256-GCM.

nodes.label: Ravenroot Configurator
nodes.rationale: Standalone Node 24 component that packages guided operator configuration into a portable .rrcfg and applies it to an existing Ravenroot deployment without building source.

nodes.label: Durable Hold Record
nodes.rationale: First-class record stored beside the process instance that identifies which WAITING state is a deliberate hold, distinct from lifecycle status.

nodes.label: Qualifying Hold Boundary
nodes.rationale: Point between two dispatches where continuation is durably expressible: single branch, single completed node, no fan-in, no iteration lap, structured payload.

nodes.label: Recovery Behavior for Held Traversals
nodes.rationale: Held traversals produce no claimable work, so recovery leaves them held; only explicit authorized resume continues them.

nodes.label: WAITING Lifecycle Status
nodes.rationale: Existing status reused for holds to avoid extending the per-instance status vocabulary; outranks INTERRUPTED for recovery classification.

nodes.label: ADR 0007: Process Traversal Invocation Attempt Lifecycle
nodes.norm_label: adr 0007: process traversal invocation attempt lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Defines lifecycle levels and statuses; its aggregate enforces that no invocation is added to a non-RUNNING traversal.

nodes.label: ADR 0031: Durable Canonical Graph Definitions
nodes.rationale: Provides pinned graph version stored in the hold continuation.

nodes.label: ADR 0032: Durable Process Inventory is Authoritative Rows
nodes.norm_label: adr 0032: durable process inventory is authoritative rows
nodes.rationale: Sets retention rules for rows and derived recovery classification; held instances report WAITING and are excluded from restart-recovery cohort.

nodes.label: ADR 0033: Durable Operator Holds on Traversals
nodes.norm_label: adr 0033: durable operator holds on traversals
nodes.rationale: Accepted decision making traversal holds durable records rather than process-local state, ensuring restart-safe pause/resume semantics.

nodes.label: ADR Status Vocabulary
nodes.rationale: Accepted does not imply implemented; Superseded in part keeps unsuperseded portions authoritative; Superseded retained for history.

nodes.label: ADR Curation Manifest
nodes.rationale: Records publication status and relationship of every decision; working proposals enter only when ready for publication.

nodes.label: Durable canonical graph definitions (ADR 0031)
nodes.rationale: Accepted durable canonical graph definitions for accepted executions.

nodes.label: Engine supervision, cancellation, and drain (ADR 0012)
nodes.rationale: Accepted supervision and termination contract for the engine.

nodes.label: Execution-engine abstraction and runtime selection (ADR 0002)
nodes.rationale: Accepted core abstraction for execution engines and runtime selection.

nodes.label: Explicit Workspaces and runner coordinators (ADR 0042)
nodes.rationale: Accepted; supersedes ADR 0041 governed workspace-agent runner plane.

nodes.label: Process, traversal, invocation, and attempt lifecycle (ADR 0007)
nodes.norm_label: process, traversal, invocation, and attempt lifecycle (adr 0007)
nodes.rationale: Accepted lifecycle contract governing process/traversal/invocation/attempt.

nodes.label: Ravenroot ADR Collection
nodes.rationale: Definitive public record of Ravenroot architecture decisions; independently browsable from docs/.

nodes.label: Artifact Provenance Setting
nodes.rationale: Defaults to 'unverified', explicitly declaring the absence of verification checks for local development.

nodes.label: Audit Trail Directory
nodes.rationale: Points to persistent volume to ensure fsync'd audit trail survives restarts, unlike tmpfs.

nodes.label: Ravenroot Audit Data Volume
nodes.rationale: Named volume for durable storage of audit, execution store, and artifact store data.

nodes.label: GraalPy Resource Cache Path
nodes.rationale: Set to persistent volume to allow GraalPy standard library extraction, preventing ModuleNotFoundError.

nodes.label: Dual Control Setting
nodes.rationale: Inverted to false to allow single-principal approval in local dev, bypassing the 403 error for workbench steps.

nodes.label: Graal Sandbox Supervisor Path
nodes.rationale: Hard-coded container path to avoid host environment leakage; satisfies supervisor contract without isolation.

nodes.label: Container Security Hardening
nodes.rationale: Includes read_only root, cap_drop ALL, no-new-privileges, and pids_limit to restrict container capabilities.

nodes.label: Ravenroot Development Compose Configuration
nodes.rationale: Declares a genuine local-only development mode with specific security and persistence trade-offs.

nodes.label: Change Fragments
nodes.rationale: Markdown files under .changes/ that record release-note entries and version increment requirements for user-visible changes.

nodes.label: Dev Integration Branch
nodes.rationale: The active development branch where all feature, fix, docs, and test branches must be based and merged.

nodes.label: Documentation Policy
nodes.rationale: Rules for documentation contributions including audience selection, page types, English-only canonical contract, and editorial review.

nodes.label: Main Release Branch
nodes.rationale: Represents the latest released product state; protected and reserved for internal dev and hotfix merges.

nodes.label: Public Contracts
nodes.rationale: GraphML, HTTP, event, CLI, extension, persistence, and configuration interfaces that must not be silently broken.

nodes.label: Release Classification Labels
nodes.rationale: Labels (release:none, patch, minor, major) used by maintainers to classify pull requests to main and determine versioning.

nodes.label: Release Preparation Process
nodes.rationale: The workflow for collecting approved changes on dev, creating a release PR to main, and passing the release gate.

nodes.label: Contributing to Ravenroot
nodes.rationale: Defines the contribution workflow, branch strategy, and public contract preservation rules for the Ravenroot project.

nodes.label: Kubernetes Runner Helm Template
nodes.rationale: Defines the complete Kubernetes runner plane: per-pool namespaces, RBAC, network isolation, resource quotas, and admission policies for attested agent workloads.

nodes.label: Manager RBAC Role
nodes.rationale: Grants the manager service account limited permissions: CRUD on pods/PVCs and create/get on pods/exec, with fixed attestation entry points.

nodes.label: Network Control Deployment
nodes.rationale: Minimal Python socket listener on port 9443 that accepts and immediately closes connections, serving as the bootstrap network control endpoint.

nodes.label: Network Policy (Bootstrap Control)
nodes.rationale: Implements one-way network bootstrap: attesting pods can only egress to the network-control service on port 9443, and the control service only accepts ingress from attesting pods.

nodes.label: Pod Disruption Budget
nodes.rationale: Ensures at least one worker pod remains available during voluntary disruptions.

nodes.label: Resource Quota (Bounded Workload)
nodes.rationale: Bounds the workload namespace with max pods, PVCs, and storage to prevent resource exhaustion.

nodes.label: Validating Admission Policy (Pod)
nodes.rationale: Enforces strict pod creation constraints: single agent container, immutable image, non-root security context, guaranteed QoS, bounded environment, and complete ownership annotations.

nodes.label: Validating Admission Policy (Exec Channel)
nodes.rationale: Restricts pods/exec CONNECT operations to only the audited attestation and agent runtime entry points with bounded parameters.

nodes.label: Evidence Profile Budget Ceilings
nodes.rationale: Reproducible evidence profile numeric ceilings for definition bytes, depth, states, transitions, input tokens, work units, and trace entries.

nodes.label: Implementation Sequence and Gates
nodes.rationale: Four-stage sequence from architecture evidence through universal package, authoring, and determinization with test gates.

nodes.label: NodeFailurePayload Contract
nodes.rationale: Contains exactly nodeId, errorClass, message, and input; unwraps deepest cause for stable diagnostics.

nodes.label: RetryClassifier Integration
nodes.rationale: Honors explicit Retryability.DETERMINISTIC_REJECT classification before author-supplied retry allowlist.

nodes.label: Typed Exception Categories
nodes.rationale: Future adapter uses distinct exception types for definition, input, and limit failures with RetryClassified contract.

nodes.label: Authoring and Later Stages Roadmap
nodes.rationale: Outlines deferred authoring features including determinization, minimization, subset construction, and implementation sequence gates.

nodes.label: Integration and Algorithm Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Specifies NodePackage/NodeBehavior integration, complexity bounds for DFA/NFA execution, and separation of parser/validator/model/executor responsibilities.

nodes.label: Validation, Failure and Governance Contract
nodes.rationale: Defines static validation, typed failure categories, FA_* diagnostic codes, and deployment-owned budget ceilings for finite automata.

nodes.label: Agent Runtime & Deterministic Conformance
nodes.rationale: agent_runtime.py speaks bounded line-delimited model/tool protocol to supervisor; deterministic conformance image is not Agent acceptance evidence; secretless native CI loopback.

nodes.label: Commands & Graph Routing
nodes.rationale: Standard commands (plan, read, research, review, implement, test, remediate, integrate, resume, summarize, handoff); graph construction checks named catalog declaration; remediation routing.

nodes.label: Runner Plane HTTP Surface (/v1/runner-plane)
nodes.rationale: Catalog, register, assignments, availability, health, audit, workspaces, jobs, artifacts endpoints with fencing and revision-CAS.

nodes.label: Runner Identity Chain
nodes.rationale: processInstanceId → traversalId → invocationId → attemptId → runnerJobId; no runner chooses these IDs.

nodes.label: RunnerCodec Binary Envelope
nodes.rationale: Length-bounded binary format with version magic, SHA-256 corruption detection, 16 MiB doc / 1 MiB payload bounds; not Java serialization.

nodes.label: Runner SPI (RunnerDriver, RunnerAssignment, RunnerRegistration, RunnerResult, RunnerWorkspaceRelease)
nodes.norm_label: runner spi (runnerdriver, runnerassignment, runnerregistration, runnerresult, runnerworkspacerelease)
nodes.rationale: Core versioned service provider interface types that form the runner contract.

nodes.label: Workspace Lifecycle & Scoping
nodes.rationale: PROCESS_INSTANCE, PER_WORKSPACE, PER_INVOCATION scoping; quiescent handoff; no second Agent-to-Agent lease.

nodes.label: Governed Runner Protocol v1
nodes.rationale: Defines the versioned runner SPI, identity chain, workspace lifecycle, HTTP surface, binary codec, and command routing for governed runners.

nodes.label: Assistant Consent Store
nodes.rationale: Per-author consent is durable in its own SQLite file (ravenroot-assistant-consent.db) and fails closed if unreadable.

nodes.label: Assistant Credential Model
nodes.rationale: Selects between api-key and oauth credential sources with no fallback; OAuth tokens are process-local and require reconnection after restart.

nodes.label: Assistant Egress Policy
nodes.rationale: Operator-owned outbound allowlist (hosts/ports) and local-HTTP exception; a provider and credential without this setting remain inert.

nodes.label: Assistant Environment Configuration
nodes.rationale: All assistant settings are read from process environment at startup; changes require restart and are not persisted through the API.

nodes.label: Authoring Assistant Service
nodes.rationale: The workspace service behind /v1/assistant; its provider profile is deployment configuration separate from llm-prompt and agent node profiles.

nodes.label: Assistant Status Route
nodes.rationale: GET /v1/assistant returns configuration, allowlist, and link status used for availability diagnosis.

nodes.label: Local OpenAI-Compatible Provider Setup
nodes.rationale: Procedure for a credential-free local chat-completions endpoint using localhost and the local-HTTP opt-in.

nodes.label: Authoring Assistant Operator Guide
nodes.rationale: Primary document describing the /v1/assistant workspace service, its immutable startup configuration, provider profiles, and operational flows.

nodes.label: AMQP Acceptance Exercise
nodes.rationale: Sanitized real-runtime acceptance exercise via `pnpm example:amqp`; builds AMQP with plugin.sh, packages closed bytes, starts RabbitMQ and Ravenroot through Compose, proves container recreation, verifies readiness and live amqp.publish/amqp.consume catalog, plans idempotent reapply, verifies compensation.

nodes.label: Bundle Integrity Verification
nodes.rationale: Packaging verifies version-one plugin manifest, ravenroot.node-sdk/2 contract, declared filenames, sizes, SHA-256 digests, and absence of undeclared files; applying a package never calls a source build or plugin.sh.

nodes.label: Kubernetes Planning and Verification
nodes.rationale: Kubernetes planning queries live Deployment, direct and envFrom sources, and generated configuration Secret; unavailable or malformed cluster state fails closed; offline operation limited to inspect; verification requires generated Secret data, direct Secret references, document Secret volumes/mounts, selected bundle image, deployed Helm release, and available rollout.

nodes.label: Plan, Apply, and Recover Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Operational flow: plan against intended target directory, apply confined to .ravenroot-config/, durable journal and recovery snapshot before external mutation, compensation in reverse order on failure, rollback completes pending interrupted transactions.

nodes.label: Publication Boundary Policy
nodes.rationale: Operator-owned closed version-one JSON file (RAVENROOT_PUBLICATION_POLICY_CONFIG) containing immutable policy IDs/versions, candidate byte ceilings, and ordered declarative rules; unset retains fail-closed empty resolver; policy decisions written to durable audit trail without candidate content.

nodes.label: .rrcfg Version-One Package
nodes.rationale: Version-one ZIP artifact produced by `ravenroot-config pack`; manifest reports target binding, tenant identities, selected contracts, required capabilities, bundle identities/digests, entry digests, and a redacted change plan; secret values never appear in the plan.

nodes.label: Secret Handling and Credential References
nodes.rationale: Target-owned credentials remain references (Compose env var, Kubernetes Secret+key); embedded values accepted only via process environment named by pack spec, package password from stdin, encrypted with Argon2id and AES-256-GCM; JSON uses {"$secret": "binding-id"} placeholder substituted during apply.

nodes.label: Configuration Packager
nodes.rationale: Standalone operator tool that produces a single reviewable .rrcfg artifact for Ravenroot profiles, backend policy, credentials, and optional prebuilt node packages; explicitly does not build Ravenroot or invoke plugin.sh.

nodes.label: Runner Job Continuation Uncertainty Resolution
nodes.rationale: RUNNER_JOB_CONTINUATION_UNCERTAIN marker with three dispositions: RESUME, ACKNOWLEDGE, ABANDON; requires same-tenant control authority, exact revision, and process fence.

nodes.label: Governed Runner Process Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Authoritative process lifecycle over runner delivery; defines QUEUED/CLAIMED/UNKNOWN states, fenced heartbeats, reconciliation, and cancellation semantics.

nodes.label: Process Control API Contract
nodes.rationale: POST /v1/processes/{processInstanceId}/{command} requires Idempotency-Key and X-Ravenroot-Expected-Generation; pause/stop/resume/cancel semantics with revision-based conflict resolution.

nodes.label: Retention, Backup and Rollback Policy
nodes.rationale: Terminal inventory retention, cleanup authority, database/workspace/artifact backup consistency, SQLite/PostgreSQL migration constraints, and rollback drain requirements.

nodes.label: Runner Observability Metrics
nodes.rationale: OpenTelemetry metrics: ravenroot.runner.observations enum, worker active/capacity/available gauges, recovery_page gauges; process-local observations not durable totals.

nodes.label: Runner Quota Acceptance Fixture
nodes.rationale: scripts/fixtures/runner_quota_acceptance.py: bounded 4GiB XFS file, isolated classic-overlay2 daemon, private bridge, secretless profile, deterministic tool proposals; refuses local/self-hosted environments.

nodes.label: Verification and Acceptance Contract
nodes.rationale: Daemon-backed read-only/reconciliation/cleanup test, writable development-cycle acceptance, hermetic model-protocol endpoint fixture, and live-provider owner-only smoke test.

nodes.label: Workspace Storage v3 Migration
nodes.rationale: Adds explicit resources and ownership generations; adapters retain legacy v1/v2 reading; process control state persisted under revision/CAS; RECOVERY_REQUIRED state for unknowable compacted prefixes.

nodes.label: Workbench CSP frame-src Derivation
nodes.rationale: CSP frame-src list is derived exclusively from registered origins; absent registry yields frame-src 'none', and browser/request origins never widen it.

nodes.label: Override Scope and Audit Requirements
nodes.rationale: ravenroot.human-task.override restricted to TENANT_ADMIN or PLATFORM_ADMIN; every override carries operator reason and produces separate audit evidence; not for routine responder workflows.

nodes.label: Responder Enforcement Configuration Flag
nodes.rationale: humanTask.responderEnforcementEnabled (Helm) or RAVENROOT_HUMAN_TASK_RESPONDER_ENFORCEMENT_ENABLED (env) toggles enforcement; effective value verified via GET /v1/configuration.

nodes.label: Admin Attention/Settlement Override Routes
nodes.rationale: Tenant-explicit admin routes for review override; only platform admin may select another tenant; override requires operator reason and produces separate audit evidence.

nodes.label: Capability Revocation and Upgrade Path
nodes.rationale: SQLite/PostgreSQL upgrades add presentation columns and capability revocations automatically; old rows remain classic tasks; requires backup, readiness check, and cross-replica revocation test before restoring traffic.

nodes.label: Human Task Authorization Model
nodes.rationale: Tenant-local authorization with optional responder enforcement; fresh deployments leave enforcement disabled, requiring explicit Helm/env configuration to require graph-authored roles and scopes.

nodes.label: Presentation Host Interaction Registry
nodes.rationale: Closed registry stored in secret-managed read-only file; drives Workbench CSP frame-src derivation and capability issuance for custom/external presentation profiles.

nodes.label: Inventory and Reconciliation Operations
nodes.rationale: Admin API for payload-free task classification (actionable, terminal, orphaned, non-resumable); CANCEL performs graph re-entry while FORCE_ABANDON atomically closes handler/timers/traversal without re-entry.

nodes.label: Deployment Lifecycle Records
nodes.rationale: SQLite deployment registry adds four tables (aggregate, graph versions, lease, command ledger) co-located with execution store; ownership is enforced via lease and fencing counter evaluated against store clock.

nodes.label: Durable Execution Results
nodes.rationale: Terminal results are stored in the configured store keyed by tenant and traversal, surviving restarts and enabling multi-instance reads; cache is not consulted for terminal answers to respect retention deadlines.

nodes.label: Durable Holds for Paused Traversals
nodes.rationale: A hold is committed atomically with the WAITING state transition, ensuring no gap between held state and its record; recovery cannot dispatch held work, only explicit resume or cancel can continue it.

nodes.label: Multi-Instance Sharing Limitations
nodes.rationale: SQLite cross-process exclusion relies on POSIX advisory locks, unreliable over network filesystems; host-local only, no live subscription across instances.

nodes.label: Payload Withheld States
nodes.rationale: WITHHELD payloadState distinguishes store byte cap exceeded (non-zero size) from runtime payload limits rejection (zero size); zero-size is the common case, and raising store cap does not help when runtime limits rejected the value.

nodes.label: Store Schema Upgrade Rules
nodes.rationale: Upgrades are additive only (new tables, no alterations); downgrades are refused, requiring backup before upgrade; stores without durable hold capability retain process-local behavior.

nodes.label: Timed Joins During Holds
nodes.rationale: Join timeouts measure active execution time only; hold duration is excluded from the deadline, and the remaining budget is preserved across pause/resume cycles.

nodes.label: Post-Recovery Verification
nodes.rationale: After recovery, verify /ready, retained results, event cursors, and bounded Test graph execution; confirm process instance discoverability and read disposition (PARKED vs terminal) rather than only lifecycle status.

nodes.label: Durable Result Store Semantics
nodes.rationale: Keeps the first recorded terminal outcome for a given execution id and never overwrites; resubmission does not change the result.

nodes.label: GET /v1/executions/{id} HTTP Route
nodes.rationale: Returns visitedNodes as unique membership; lexical sort is not visit order; 410 and 404 conditions match CLI result.

nodes.label: ravenroot deployments command
nodes.rationale: Manages local runtimes; Stop requires --reason, Undeploy requires --disposition and --reason.

nodes.label: ravenroot inventory command
nodes.rationale: Maps to GET /v1/executions/inventory; internally follows nextCursor to completion, always includes terminal rows, and prints retained-from.

nodes.label: ravenroot process command
nodes.rationale: Applies durable process commands (Pause, Resume, Cancel, Drain, Stop) via remote server; prints typed outcome, generation, state, and retained reason.

nodes.label: ravenroot result command
nodes.rationale: Presents visitedNodes as unique membership; prints termination-reason only when qualified; reports 410 EXECUTION_RESULT_EXPIRED/REDACTED and 404 UNKNOWN_EXECUTION.

nodes.label: ravenroot traversals command
nodes.rationale: Maps to GET /v1/executions/{id}/traversals; not paginated; prints retained-from.

nodes.label: CLI to HTTP Resource Mapping

nodes.label: Deployment Command Outcomes

nodes.label: Deployment Lifecycle Contract

nodes.label: Execution and Events Contract
nodes.rationale: Defines execution lifecycle, durable result store, process instance vs traversal ID distinction, and SSE event streams.

nodes.label: Governed Resources Contract

nodes.label: Process Instance ID Space

nodes.label: Node Attempt
nodes.rationale: Execution unit that may produce zero or more emissions; retried as a whole; completion settled once before routing.

nodes.label: Bounded Per-Attempt Ceiling
nodes.rationale: Rejects the whole attempt when emission count exceeds the ceiling, preventing silent data loss.

nodes.label: Exactly-One Compatibility Baseline
nodes.rationale: Existing exactly-one emission behavior remains representation-compatible with the new zero-or-more contract.

nodes.label: Emission

nodes.label: NodeResult SPI
nodes.rationale: Public SPI that constrains implementation; the ADR does not authorize binary contract changes without separate approval.

nodes.label: Routing Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Per-emission routing logic; partial failure is explicit and cannot rewrite settled node results.

nodes.label: ADR 0030: Zero or More Node Emissions

nodes.rationale: Accepted contract allowing a node attempt to produce an ordered list of zero or more emissions, each with independent routing, to support splitters without hiding routing logic in payloads.

nodes.label: Cancellation as Termination Reason
nodes.rationale: Records cancelled executions as FAILED with a nullable CANCELLED reason to preserve exhaustive switch compatibility, while publishing a distinct EXECUTION_CANCELLED event.

nodes.label: Durable Journal
nodes.rationale: The authoritative source for replay and recovery, distinct from the ring buffer which serves bounded recent delivery.

nodes.label: Recovery Invariant
nodes.rationale: Recovery reconstructs accepted work from durable authority; live delivery accelerates observation but never substitutes for stored truth.

nodes.label: Ring Buffer
nodes.rationale: Serves bounded recent delivery, acting as a cache for live observation rather than a storage authority.

nodes.label: Terminal Result States
nodes.rationale: Defines four distinct states for retained results (produced-and-kept, refused-for-size, unrepresentable, never produced) and a Redacted read state, avoiding nullable fields.
